column1: # Shiren GB — translation file. Keyed on `loc`, one string per line.
# READ `TRANSLATING.md` FIRST. It covers the three storage classes, the measured
# per-renderer Dot Gothic limits, the character set, control tokens, and every error
# build/worklist.tsv can print. `VWF_BUDGETS.md` is the canonical fit register.
# KEY IS `loc` (bank:$addr), never the sequential id: ids are reassigned by sorted
# offset, so any change to extraction silently shifts an id-keyed file by one entry.
# Length: these are almost all table-referenced, so storage is not the limit — the tool
# relocates them. Display limits are measured per path: pixels, source staging, temporary
# tiles, and runtime substitutions. Do not infer one universal character/cell budget.
# V4C restores boxes 6/39 to the Japanese x=13,w=5 geometry. Byte 0 remains the raw
# cursor cell, while the proportional reader scans the complete staged verb and paints
# it into the remaining 32px. `Remove` is the exact-edge 40px row including the cursor.
# Recovered 2026-07-29: the pointer table was being read as 15 entries, so these three were
# invisible. They are LIVE -- ひろう and だす come from the category tables at 30:$7E14 and
# $7E40, はずす from the equip/remove substitution at 30:$7D73.
# One line per BOX ROW. The rows of a box are one allocation, so a box that anything
# points at can grow; box 2 is pinned (see script.json `box.pinned`) and each of its rows
# is limited to its original cell count.
# These addresses used to be a byte-count guess away from the truth: 31:$41E2 and
# 31:$4414 were the DESCRIPTOR of the box below them, and the translation had to carry
# six or eight <$XX> layout bytes to step over it. Now that box_descriptors() finds the
# real row starts, the descriptor is data again and the text begins where it says.
# 31:$41F6 is a composite: two labels sharing one row, split by the vertical bar glyph
# $B6. The <$B6> token emits that byte verbatim so the column layout survives.
# Box 1 is 11 cells and the VALUE is drawn right-aligned on the row BELOW its label
# (screenshot: "Gld" then "0G" beneath it), so the label has all 11 cells to itself.
# There was no reason for three-letter abbreviations here.
# なんいど = 難易度, "difficulty level". The game calls its difficulty choices dungeon
# paths elsewhere, so "Path" is both compact and consistent with that terminology.
# The tool prepends the cursor space itself where the original row starts with one, so
# these are one cell narrower than the box. "Normal" needs a 7-wide box; the cursor follows
# the box now, so it fits.
# One line per box ROW. Budgets come from two places and both are checked:
#   - the box `width` (box_geometry.tsv overrides it) -- how much the drawer will draw
#   - for a PINNED box, the original cell count -- pinned rows cannot grow, because a
#     second reader points into the middle of the block and relocating it would leave
#     that pointer stale. `pinned` is in script.json under each row's `box`.
# ---- inventory titles (each its own one-row box) ----
# ---- item categories: box 33 consumables, box 34 equipment ----
# HELD BACK -- these do not fit, and not for want of total space. Bank 31's descriptors sit
# between the text blocks, so its free pool is a set of runs of at most 26 bytes, and these
# two boxes need 32 and 38 contiguous. build.py reports it as fragmentation, not shortfall.
# The 116 contiguous bytes of the katakana grid page are what unlocks them; see HANDOFF.md.
# Uncomment together with a width of 7 for both boxes in box_geometry.tsv.
# These use their measured box shapes and approved proportional pixels. `build.py` checks the
# source row; `fontaudit.py` and the menu spill tests check physical width and allocation.
# `だい   もん  なんいど` is `Question No. _` + `Difficulty`, and TWO other bits of code
# write into this row. Both columns were MEASURED off the screen's own tilemap rather
# than guessed, after the first attempt put `Difficulty` over one of them:
#   cells 2-4   the task number, right-aligned (a `1` landed on cell 4)
#   cell 13+    the difficulty stars (tile $8A, which is not a font tile at all)
# So the label has cells 7-12 -- six -- and `Difficulty` needs ten. `Rating` is the
# reading that fits a star row and does not collide with Shiren's own `Lv`.
# ---- title screen: start menu, rankings, dungeon entrances ----
# "Kuyou Pass" would make this box 26 bytes, and the only 26-byte run in bank 31 is the
# one box 33 needs. 26+24 into 26+23 does not fit however it is ordered.
# Row 2 of each is centred by hand in the original; one leading space is re-added, the
# rest is up to the text.
# ~~Box 48 is NOT translatable in place.~~ It is, as of 2026-08-05. It was never the
# 20-bytes-in-an-18-cell-box arithmetic that blocked it -- that only bites a row that
# cannot MOVE, and box 48 was only immovable because extraction pinned it by mistake.
# `31:$755B ld bc,$4571 / call $028B` is a message-queue push, so `$4571` is a BANK 13
# address (`<cE0:2B>とっぷうだ！！`), not a pointer into this block. box_interior_targets
# now asks msg_push_kind before believing an operand. Boxes 50 and 51 came unpinned with
# it. Joey reported this screen, and he was right that no text location should be
# ---- name-entry page label + menu words (boxes 12 and 13, row 0) ----
# The three words are SELECTABLE, and the picker maps cursor positions to columns, so
# these keep the original column layout exactly: label at 0-3, then 6-8, 10-12, 15-17.
# Moving them would move what the cursor lands on.
# Box 13 -- the second page -- is now ALIASED to box 12 in script/box_alias.tsv, so it has
# no rows of its own to translate and this key would match no string. Its 116 bytes are
# what let the item category boxes keep "Staff". The old page branch still resolves to
# this same grid, but the visible toggle action is retired because there is no second
# Ten real composer lines, chosen from a `msglog.py` transcript so every one is text the
# game demonstrably draws, and covering the three shapes the sample had to cover:
# combat fragments with runtime substitutions, a speaker-prefixed village line, and one
# long multi-box conversation. This was the original POC sample; production dialogue now
# uses the measured 30-source-glyph/144px Dot contract in `VWF_BUDGETS.md`.

# Control codes are written by NAME (``, `
`, ``), the same tokens
# codec.decode prints in script.tsv's `jp` column. Do NOT spell them `<$E2>`: an escape
# means "layout byte, reserve it out of the DTE code space", and a control code is
# ---- combat fragments (bank 13, relocatable, and already DTE-allowlisted) ----
# These are FRAGMENTS assembled at render time, not sentences: `<var>` pulls a name from
# the message queue and `<cE4>` a number, so each pair below draws as two lines of one
# box. Japanese orders them "X wa Y ni / dealt <cE4> points of damage"; English keeps the
# same split, with the verb on line 1 and the number on line 2, so no fragment boundary
# Runtime substitutions share the same source and pixel canvas as the literal text.
# `fontaudit.py` reports unknown-producer variants separately; no 14/16-cell guess is a
# The compact wording leaves room for the runtime name; exact producer/value measurement,
# not the old fixed-cell count, decides whether a longer alternative is safe.
# Keep the compact `Lv` terminology while the `<var>` producer census remains open.
# ---- hunger warnings (bank 13; the last two are IN-PLACE and byte-capped) ----
# $45DF has 19 bytes and $45F3 has 16, and neither is DTE-allowlisted, so those two are
# hard byte limits with no compression to spend. "About to collapse!" is 20 bytes with
# the <cE0:88> prefix and does not fit; "Ready to drop!" does.
# ---- village dialogue (bank 14, ALL in-place: the pointer is computed at runtime, so
# these cannot be repointed and must fit their original byte count exactly) ----
# The speaker prefix is where the budget goes. `おかみ「` is 4 bytes; `Innkeeper: ` is 11.
# The font has no `"` glyph (available punctuation is  !'()+,-./:?[]~ ), so attribution
# is `Name: ` with no quotes -- which is also 2 bytes cheaper than 「...」 would have been.

column1: # SESSION 4a — BANK 13 SYSTEM TEXT (Dot composer: 30 glyphs / 144px, 3 lines)
# These are FRAGMENTS the message queue assembles at runtime, not sentences. Adjacent
# addresses draw as consecutive LINES of one box, so a pair whose Japanese dangles on a
# particle -- `<cE3>を`, `<cE3>は`, `なんと！ アイテムは` -- has to dangle in English too
# and be completed by the next entry. Every such pair is marked `+` below.
# BUDGETS. Runtime substitutions consume their actual source glyphs and Dot pixels inside
# the same 30/144 line. The former 14-cell `<var>` and 16-cell `<cE3>` reservations are
# historical audit warnings, not wording limits. Known item suffixes are enumerated
# exactly; the remaining producer-to-template census stays visible in `fontaudit.py`.
# THERE IS NO `%` GLYPH (the set is  !'()+,-./:?[]~ ), so the fullness messages say
# `is now <cE6>.` and drop the sign rather than spell out `pct`.
# ---- hunger (the four warnings above are TASK 2's and already reviewed) ----
# ---- picking things up, putting them down ----
# `Got` remains the concise established pickup wording. The renderer itself now accepts
# up to 30 source glyphs and 144 painted pixels; exact item variants are audited.

column1: # ---- the suspend-and-resume notice (three lines of one box) ----
# `「ぼうけんにでる」` is quoted in the Japanese; there is no `"` glyph, and the menu entry
# it names is `Adventure` (11:$5330), so it is referred to by name instead.
# SESSION 4b — ITEM DESCRIPTIONS (Dot help path: 21 glyphs / 144px, 4 lines)
# A DIFFERENT RENDERER AND A DIFFERENT BUDGET. These 122 strings are reached through
# `13:$554A`, staged by `13:$7E49` into `$C616` and drawn by bank 31 as box 7 -- x=0, y=3,
# five rows of 18 tiles. Row 1 is the item NAME, so descriptions get four 144px rows.
# Menu VWF accepts 21 source glyphs per row. `dialogue_preview.py <loc>` checks both the
# source guard and exact Dot painted extent.
# `<brk>` IS A PAGE, and the page count is kept identical to the Japanese on purpose --
# the unit selector at `13:$7E0D` counts `$EE`/`$FF` markers to page forward, so a page
# added or dropped changes what the player can reach. Tighten the English instead.
# `<cF0:xx>` PASTES ONE OF THE 13 SHARED LINES from `11:$55AC` inline at that point --
# it is text, not a screen effect, and spends its own source glyphs and pixels. They are
# translated at the bottom of this block. `<cF0:03>` (`When equipped:`) uses its own row.
# Identity-hidden items do NOT select one of these rows. With `$CF7B` bit 7 clear,
# `13:$7E0D` returns the directly embedded fallback at `13:$5537`. It has no pointer-table
# reference and therefore no TSV key; `tools/itemfix.py` safely replaces its exact 18-byte
# Japanese sentence with `Effect is unknown.` for every appearance/category.
# The same formatter copies a second direct literal from `4:$5773` into the preceding
# title row; its 11-byte `みしきべつのアイテム` becomes the compact heading `Unknown`.

column1: # ---- the 13 shared lines `<cF0:xx>` pastes in (bank 11, table 11:$55AC) ----
# These are not menu labels: each is inline item-help text under the 21-source-glyph and
# ---- SESSION 9: the equipment SEALS (印), bank 11, table 11:$5463, 20 entries ----
# What a player sees on the item screen under a weapon or shield that has been melded.
# `4:$49F5` zeroes $78 bytes at $C616, `4:$5736` stages the item NAME into row 1, then
# `11:$7E40` walks the item's seal ids at $C6BE and copies up to FOUR of these in behind
# it (`ld c,$04`), terminator included. `4:$4A0D` draws box $13 -- whose descriptor
# (31:$4395) is byte for byte box 7's, the item-description box.
# PRODUCTION BUDGET: one 21-source-glyph/144px Dot line per seal. The four rows are shared

# out one per seal, so a `
` here would eat the next seal's row. The native Japanese
# control still has 18 fixed cells. `dialogue_preview.is_seal` selects the real check.
# WORDING IS TAKEN FROM THE ITEM DESCRIPTIONS ABOVE, which describe the same effects at
# greater length and are already reviewed -- `Deals heavy damage to Dragons` (13:$56C1),
# `To one-eyed foes` (13:$57E2), `To foes that drain your stats` (13:$57F6), `Your attacks
# never miss` (13:$5793), `Lands critical hits often` (13:$57A9), `Never rusts` (13:$58CD),
# `Cuts damage from explosions` (13:$5A2C). A seal and its description must not read like
# `Dragons` / `Ghosts` / `One-Eyes` are capitalised as monster FAMILIES, the way 13:$56C1
# and 13:$5736 already do; `dragon fire` stays lowercase, the way 13:$58EB already does.
# The game does not explain these two -- it just names the seal in quote marks. Neither is
# an item in the glossary, so there is nothing to align to and nothing to expand into. The
# font has no `"` (the set is  !'()+,-./:?[]~ ), so the corner brackets become square ones.
# ---- the one item name with a LEADING SPACE, and why ----
# Gitan is item category 11, and `4:$5C6A` puts the COUNT before the name for that category
# (and for arrows) instead of after it, with no separator -- correct for `293ギタン`, wrong
# for English. The count is emitted by `4:$5CAB`, which has no spare byte after its digits
# and no free run in bank 4 to relocate into, so the separator lives in the name instead.
# This is an override of the frozen glossary's `Gitan` (11:$452C) and the only one of its
# kind. It fixes the message AND the item-list row, because both reach the same builder.
# The arrow half of the same bug IS patched in code -- see tools/itemfix.py, which had the
# two bytes to work with because it was replacing a counter word rather than inserting one.
